skill.name: iac-checkov
skill.description: Guides Infrastructure as Code security reviews with Checkov for Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Dockerfile, Helm, and related CI workflows.
skill.summary: Run Checkov IaC scans, CI gates, custom policies, and compliance reports.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from documentation examples, Checkov templates, local CI report parsing, and security training text. No prompt-injection attempts or credential disclosure were found in the reviewed files. Two contextual supply-chain improvements remain for pinned GitHub Actions and trusted external custom policies.

remediation.issue: Mutable GitHub Action reference in workflow examples.
remediation.suggestion: Pin bridgecrewio/checkov-action to a release tag or commit SHA and document the update process.

remediation.issue: External custom policy repository example lacks trust guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to load custom policies only from reviewed repositories and pinned refs.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable GitHub Action Reference
semantic_findings.description: The workflow examples use bridgecrewio/checkov-action@master. A mutable branch reference can change CI behavior without review if the upstream branch changes or is compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced lines directly use a mutable branch for a CI action. This is a well-known supply-chain risk, although it is not evidence of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: External Custom Policy Source Needs Trust Warning
semantic_findings.description: The custom policy guide shows loading checks from a Git repository. Checkov custom Python policies should come from reviewed and pinned sources because policy code can run during scans.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide uses a placeholder organization repository, so legitimate use is likely. The missing trust and pinning warning still creates a contextual supply-chain risk.

content.value_statement: IaC misconfigurations can reach production before review. This skill guides Checkov scans, CI gates, suppressions, and compliance reporting for cloud infrastructure.
actual_capabilities: Guides Checkov scans for Terraform, Kubernetes, Dockerfile, Helm, CloudFormation, and ARM templates.
Shows CLI workflows for severity filters, output formats, baselines, and custom policy directories.
Provides CI examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and pre-commit hooks.
Explains suppression workflows with justifications, review controls, and expiration guidance.
Maps Checkov results to compliance needs such as CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC2, and NIST.
limitations: Requires Checkov and its runtime dependencies to be installed or available in CI.
Does not replace manual review of complex architecture risks or accepted exceptions.
Example policy IDs and mappings must be verified against the installed Checkov version.
Custom policies and external modules should be trusted before loading or scanning them.

use_cases.title: Add Pull Request Scans
use_cases.description: Add Checkov checks to pull requests and block risky IaC changes before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Generate scan reports and map findings to frameworks used by auditors.

use_cases.title: Build Custom Guardrails
use_cases.description: Create organization-specific Checkov policies for tags, network rules, and encryption controls.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic IaC Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a Terraform folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to run a basic Checkov review for ./terraform. Explain the top findings, affected resources, and safest remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add a CI Security Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions Checkov workflow for Terraform and Kubernetes. Fail on HIGH and CRITICAL findings and upload SARIF results.

prompt_templates.title: Review Suppression Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Checkov suppressions and propose an approval workflow with owners, expiration dates, evidence requirements, and review cadence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Custom Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Help design a custom Checkov policy for required resource tags. Include test cases, policy metadata, and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Scan Terraform for public exposure risks.
output: Prioritized findings by severity and affected resource.
Plain-language remediation steps for public access, encryption, and logging gaps.
Suggested follow-up checks for CI enforcement.

output_examples.input: Create compliance evidence for a security review.
output: Summary of passed, failed, and skipped checks by framework.
List of exceptions that need owner approval.
Recommended report formats for audit storage.
Decision guidance for whether the suppression is justified.
Required compensating controls and expiration date.

best_practices: Start with read-only scans and publish reports before enforcing blocking gates.
Fail builds only on agreed severity thresholds and track exceptions with owners.
Keep Checkov, policies, and CI templates pinned and reviewed.
anti_patterns: Do not suppress HIGH or CRITICAL findings without written approval.
Do not load custom policies from untrusted repositories.
Do not rely on soft-fail mode as the final production control.

faq.question: What does this skill scan?
faq.answer: It guides Checkov scanning for common IaC formats, including Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Dockerfile, Helm, and ARM templates.

faq.question: Does it install Checkov automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation and usage guidance. The user or CI environment must provide Checkov.

faq.question: Can it create CI workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and pre-commit workflows.

faq.question: Can it handle false positives?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains suppressions, justifications, compensating controls, and review workflows for accepted exceptions.

faq.question: Does it replace a cloud security review?
faq.answer: No. It supports automated checks, but architecture risks and business exceptions still need expert review.

faq.question: Is it useful for compliance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains reporting and mapping for frameworks such as CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC2, and NIST.
